toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The evidence points to one chance QC flag, not a faulty analyzer. The repeat of the same vial passed 21 minutes later. All other QC levels, sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 means are unchanged after the lot change. QC was run on schedule, 182 of 182 runs. Twenty-three held samples plus 20 sampled flagged results all agreed with Analyzer A within the allowable difference, and the patient median is stable. A flag like this is expected once or twice a month.

Ward 6 highs are not an analyzer issue. Half were run on Analyzer A. Most had over 3 hours' transit during the tube outage, and four renal overflow patients arrived. This is a likely, not proven, explanation.

Sign off: return Analyzer B potassium to service and close the review of the 186 results with no amendments. Do not recall about 2,900 results or widen limits, because that would hide real faults. Do not name the cause as confirmed, since a sampling glitch can't be proven. Consider extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 to send repeat samples on the high results, and push for the tube repair. Confidence is moderate to good.
